messages:
julia: new hire couldn't run the python sample CLI after I built a release wheel. pipx install <wheel> succeeds but `python -c 'import redwood'` fails with ModuleNotFoundError.

omar: can you paste the wheel filename + pyproject snippet? usually a name vs package-dir mismatch or packages not included.

julia: wheel: `dist/redwood-cli-0.4.0-py3-none-any.whl`. pyproject minimal: 
```
[tool.poetry]
name = "redwood-cli"
version = "0.4.0"

[tool.poetry.dependencies]
python = ">=3.10"

[tool.poetry.extras]
async = ["httpx", "anyio"]
```
Top-level package folder is `redwood/` (import name).

ryan_k: that lines up with the usual poetry gotcha: it assumes packages that match project name. If the package dir is `redwood` but project name is `redwood-cli` poetry might auto-create a distribution package `redwood_cli` and not include the `redwood/` dir. Run `unzip -l dist/*.whl` to inspect.

julia: did that — wheel only has `redwood_cli/__init__.py` and metadata, no `redwood/` files. pip install -e . in dev env works which is why it slipped by during local dev.

omar: two fixes: either rename the package dir to match project name (bad UX for imports) or make packages explicit in pyproject: `packages = [{"include": "redwood"}]` under [tool.poetry]. Also add `include = ["redwood/**", "py.typed"]` so typing info and package data get into the wheel.

ryan_k: another wrinkle: pipx sometimes installs from a cached wheel or fetches from our internal artifact storage which might have an old build. use `pipx install --force --verbose dist/*.whl` or `pip install --no-cache-dir dist/*.whl` in a fresh venv to be sure.

julia: downstream teams also reported that `pipx` installation didn't bring optional deps (async extra) — they expected httpx to be present. Is that expected?

omar: yes, wheel metadata includes extras, but installing a plain wheel via pipx won't install extras unless bracket notation used (e.g., `pip install redwood-cli[async]`). When distributing a CLI with optional features, document the extras or provide a metapackage. Also `poetry export` can drop extras if used without the right flags.

julia: had a mypy error in the consumer after installing the wheel: missing `py.typed` so strict downstream projects fail type checks.

ryan_k: include `py.typed` and ensure `setup.cfg`/pyproject package-data includes it. For poetry: `include = ["py.typed"]` or `package.include`.

omar: propose a small checklist and CI job for sample apps: 1) poetry build 2) unzip wheel and verify the package dir + py.typed are present 3) create fresh venv and `pip install --no-deps dist/*.whl` 4) `python -c "import redwood; print(redwood.__name__)"` 5) optional: test extras installed when expected. Fail CI if any step fails.

julia: agreed. I've opened a tiny PR to add `packages` + `include` and the CI smoke check. will post link once CI runs.

ci-bot: Created PR #501 by julia: add explicit packages mapping, include py.typed & wheel-smoke-test. CI queued. :gear: :white_check_mark:

julia: temporary workaround for the hire: `pip install -e .` or `pipx install --pip-args='-e .'` gets them unblocked. will follow up on docs for sample apps / release checklist.

ryan_k: good call. also add a short note in dev onboarding about always verifying wheel contents before tagging releases. saves time. :memo:
